verdicts.name: Sector rating LEVELS (cross-sector)
verdicts.stat: composite IC −0.03 · 7/18 years positive — worse than a coin flip
verdicts.note: THE FUND ALLOCATES ON THIS. Backtest v2 found cross-sector rating levels do not predict forward sector returns, and the paper fund still sizes positions by them (rule 1: weight ∝ rating − 4). That is now a DECLARED NULL-TEST, stated on the Fund page: we are running a documented in-sample null forward, in public, to see whether it also fails out-of-sample. Note what DID survive the same backtest — margin mean-reversion (sector-FE p=.014; 6.4% forward return after high-margin years vs 18.9% after low). The peak-earnings penalty inside the ratings is grounded; the LEVELS are not. Was recorded only in the scope doc until today.

verdicts.name: AMENDMENT 15 — vol target measured under stress correlations
verdicts.stat: reported vol 10.3% -> 20.1% · target BREACHED · scale to 75% · invested 61.3% -> ~46%
verdicts.note: RESOLVED — measurement ON, governing OFF (option A, Riley's call). The stress figure is reported on every run and does NOT scale the book. Reason: across the 9-year panel the Sharpe barely moves, 0.40 unscaled vs 0.42 scaled, so scaling is a move along the capital allocation line rather than an improvement to the portfolio — a leverage decision wearing risk-management clothes. It would have cost 1.18pt of CAGR (9.67% -> 8.49%) to buy 6.7pt of max drawdown (-27.4% -> -20.7%), which is not compelling at a paper fund with no outside capital and no forced selling. REVISIT CONDITION: external money or leverage, not a market move. Two other options were measured and rejected on evidence — a frequency-blended target gives 12.8%, still under 15%, so the 'on average' reading is ALREADY satisfied and no middle number changes behaviour; and reacting on detection is worse than it sounds, because the median drawdown episode has already fallen 14.4% before the signal fires (26.7% in 2020, with only 10.1% left to lose). Implementation note: the first version had ONE flag, so turning off the scaling would have turned off the measurement too. Split into STRESS_MEASUREMENT and STRESS_GOVERNS, because knowing the book runs 20.1% in a crisis is not an appetite question and should never have been switchable alongside one. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS. I proposed the wrong fix first and the measurement said so. After the deleveraging finding I suggested a stress-conditioned SHARE cap; measuring it showed that would have done nothing, because in DRAWDOWN the component-VaR shares CONVERGE (spread 35.6pt -> 31.3pt, top 41.8% -> 38.6%) and a 45% cap binds on nothing there. Concentration is a calm-state phenomenon. TOTAL RISK is the stressed one: the same book, unchanged weights, runs 10.3% under the trailing window and 20.1% under DRAWDOWN correlations — an 89% increase and a clear breach of a 15% target that never bound because it was estimated on ~81% calm days. Amendment 10's measured 0.227 average correlation was CORRECT and was the problem: 0.227 is a calm-state number and the book is not run in calm state alone. Under stress it is 0.549. THIS IS A RISK-APPETITE DECISION, NOT A CORRECTION. 'Target 15% vol' has two readings — 15% on average (the old behaviour, accepting ~20% in drawdowns) or 15% in all states (this, requiring a permanently smaller book). Implemented as the second because that is what the rule's own words claim, but it moves a quarter of the invested book to cash permanently and reverts with one flag. Fail-safe verified both ways: with the panel missing and with regime labels missing, it falls back to the trailing window and SAYS SO rather than printing a calm number under a stress heading.

verdicts.name: MODEL DECAY — nothing is decaying, because nothing was there
verdicts.n: 1,390 names × 83 monthly IC observations × 4 price signals
verdicts.stat: momentum IC −0.001 (t −0.03) · reversal −0.009 (t −0.63) · low-vol −0.030 (t −1.27) · low-beta −0.034 (t −1.19); no trend clears |t|=2
verdicts.note: The second failure mode from the quant-fund risk list, made measurable: does anything we run get WORSE over time? Every study before this reported a single pooled number over a decade, and a pooled zero hides two completely different situations — a signal that was +0.06 then −0.06 (decay, possibly conditionable) and one that was flat zero throughout (absence). Only a trend test separates them. Result: all four price signals are ABSENT rather than decaying. Not one has a mean IC distinguishable from zero, and not one has a downward trend clearing |t|=2. Momentum's IC actually rose across the halves (−0.025 -> +0.024) and reversal's fell (+0.015 -> −0.033), both well inside noise. This is a genuinely useful non-finding: it means the stack's negatives are NOT a crowding-and-decay story that better timing or regime conditioning could rescue. These effects were never present in this universe over this decade, which is a cleaner and more final answer than decay would have been. Fundamental signals are excluded — metrics_history is annual, and ten points cannot show a trend.

verdicts.name: DELEVERAGING RISK — amendment 14's cap is calibrated on the wrong state
verdicts.n: 2,259 labelled days · 1,827 CALM / 354 DRAWDOWN · fund 5 ETFs + 300-name universe
verdicts.stat: avg pairwise corr CALM->DRAWDOWN: fund 0.415->0.549 · universe 0.252->0.464 (nearly doubles) · risk-share spread 35.6pt->31.3pt
verdicts.note: The 'deleveraging' failure mode — synchronised selling collapsing diversification — measured rather than described. It is real: average pairwise correlation across 300 names goes from 0.252 in CALM to 0.464 in DRAWDOWN. A 1,600-name book is roughly half as diversified as it looks, in the state where that matters. THE PART THAT BEARS ON A LIVE RULE: amendment 14 caps component-VaR share at 45%, computed from the trailing year, which is overwhelmingly calm days. Recomputed by state, the shares CONVERGE under stress (spread 35.6pt -> 31.3pt) and — the uncomfortable bit — GDX's risk share FALLS from 21.9% to 16.7% while XLE's RISES from 20.6% to 26.3%. So the cap constrains the instrument that becomes relatively LESS dominant when it matters, and leaves alone the one that becomes more so. This does not invalidate amendment 14: as a normal-times concentration control it does what it was registered to do, and the registration says nothing about crises. But it should NOT be read as crisis protection, and the natural follow-up is a stress-conditioned version of the same cap. That is a new amendment and Riley's call. Measurement only — no weights changed. Note also the survivorship direction: the panel holds names listed today, so true crisis co-movement is understated and the convergence measured here is a LOWER bound.

verdicts.name: Cross-asset LEAD-LAG — the last untested structure
verdicts.n: 1,309 names · 16 sectors · 1,996 daily returns · 1.71m directed pairs deliberately NOT tested
verdicts.stat: gross +2.40bp/day t +0.88 · turnover 84%/day = 8.40bp cost · NET −5.99bp/day · 36% of months · decile rho +0.09
verdicts.note: Residual reversal asked whether a name reverts to ITSELF; this asks whether it FOLLOWS ANOTHER NAME — the last major structure the stack had not tested. 1,309 names give 1.71m directed pairs, so testing pairs individually would need |t|~5.5 and is the same trap that made pairwise cointegration indefensible. Instead ONE aggregate signal applied identically to every stock: leave-one-out mean of sector peers' PREVIOUS day, ranked cross-sectionally, long top decile short bottom. One hypothesis, one parameter set, nothing to correct for. The pre-registered prediction was 'gross weakly positive, net negative' and that is exactly what happened. Read the net t of −2.20 carefully: it is NOT evidence of an anti-signal, it is 84% daily turnover at 10bp round trip swamping a 2.4bp gross edge that was not significant to begin with. The decile means are flat from 0.01 to 0.04bp with rank correlation +0.09 — there is no ordering at all, so even the gross number is carried by extremes rather than by structure. VERIFIED, after the RMT study earlier today produced a clean null that turned out to be a non-converged optimiser: planting a lead-lag of known strength recovers it easily (k=0.05 → +14.48bp at t 5.28; k=0.20 → +50.63bp at t 18.14), so the null belongs to the data. Test 2 (peer-group size, size-direction subgroups) was pre-declared CONDITIONAL on Test 1 passing and was therefore not run.

verdicts.name: RMT covariance denoising — INCONCLUSIVE, not negative
verdicts.stat: RMT lower in 5/7 windows · 13.06% -> 12.94% realised vol (−0.9%) · paired t 0.61 · MDE 0.55pp vs a 0.13pp effect
verdicts.note: Marchenko-Pastur denoising: keep eigenvalues above λ+ = (1+√q)², replace the noise bulk with its average, preserving trace. Judged the only way that means anything — out-of-sample realised volatility of a long-only capped minimum-variance portfolio built from each matrix, walk-forward and PAIRED so both face the identical market path. Direction matches theory and matches the pre-registered prediction of a 'real but modest, single-digit' improvement: 0.9% less realised vol, lower in 5 of 7 windows. It does not clear |t|>=2. But the power calculation says the minimum detectable difference here is 0.55pp against an effect of 0.13pp — ~125 windows needed, 7 available — so this is INCONCLUSIVE, and calling it a negative would repeat the exact error the power audit found in five existing verdicts. TWO IMPLEMENTATION BUGS WERE FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THIS NUMBER WAS TRUSTED, both mine: (1) a 504-day training window gave q = N/T = 3.17, a SINGULAR matrix that Marchenko-Pastur does not describe; (2) the optimiser ran a fixed 300 iterations and silently returned a near-equal-weight vector — in-sample vol 24.00% against equal-weight's 24.52%, versus 14.00% once converged — so the first run compared two identical portfolios and reported a null. It now returns a convergence flag and windows that fail to converge are skipped rather than counted.

verdicts.name: AMENDMENT 14 — risk-share cap at 45% of component VaR
verdicts.note: Companion to amendment 13, which exposed a concentration nothing guarded: rule 3 caps CAPITAL, and for a 43.7%-vol instrument that is a different quantity from RISK. GDX sat legally at its 19.0% half-Kelly limit carrying 59% of the book's downside, and the volatility target did not bind either at 14.0% against 15%. New rule 5: no instrument above 45% of component VaR, freed capital to CASH and not redistributed — the same convention rule 3 uses. 45% was chosen from a scan of 50/45/40/35/30 because it REPRODUCES the posture the fund already had (old book 45.8% top share; this lands at 45.0%). The intent is not to change how much risk is taken but to reach the same place by a stated rule instead of a side effect. Below 40% the cap stops controlling concentration and becomes de-gearing — 35% leaves the book 44% invested — which is a different decision and was not smuggled in here. Verified: fails OPEN and loudly when the price panel is missing (weights untouched, reason logged) rather than silently returning unconstrained weights; idempotent on repeat application so it cannot ratchet the book down across runs; monotone in the threshold. Known limitation, stated up front: with five instruments and no redistribution this converts risk into cash rather than diversification, so it is a blunt tool whose main effect is de-gearing.

verdicts.name: AMENDMENT 13 — regime becomes a risk input only
verdicts.n: binds today: fund is in TENSION as of 2026-07-19
verdicts.stat: GDX 9.5% -> 19.0% (its half-Kelly cap) · invested 59.0% -> 68.5% · vol 10.1% -> 14.0% · GDX downside share 37.7% -> 59.0%
verdicts.note: Rule 4 always had two branches doing different work. Halving PRECIOUS in TENSION claims gold miners will EARN LESS — expected return. Halving the whole budget in WAR-DRAWDOWN claims the market is MORE DANGEROUS — risk. Three tests separated them: HMM kappa 0.24, K-sweep 0.342/0.217/0.127, and a zero-parameter deterministic rule with perfect stability that STILL could not separate forward returns (p=0.089) while cleanly ordering forward volatility. So the return branch is retired and the risk branch kept. This invokes the modifier's own registered off-ramp ('withdrawn or reclassified as a pure risk cap') EARLY — the three-spell test never ran, because identifying 3 confirmed TENSION spells needs a label with kappa 0.22. The premise failed, not the test. CONSEQUENCE I DID NOT ANTICIPATE AND WILL NOT BURY: removing the modifier lifts GDX to 59.0% of the book's downside risk on 27.7% of capital, and NEITHER existing guard catches it — half-Kelly is a CAPITAL cap that GDX sits legally at, and the vol target does not bind at 14.0% against 15%. The TENSION modifier had been doing risk work by accident. Amendment 13 should not ship alone; the companion is a RISK-SHARE cap on component VaR, which is a separate amendment and Riley's threshold call. Old behaviour retained behind REGIME_RISK_ONLY=False so the change is diffable.

verdicts.name: DETERMINISTIC REGIME — stable, and it still does not predict returns
verdicts.stat: stability kappa 1.000 (vs HMM 0.22) · Kruskal-Wallis on forward returns H 2.89 p 0.089 · STRESS holds 3.5% of days
verdicts.note: Third and final attempt on the regime overlay. A rule with no fitted parameters — 60d annualised vol >=25% is STRESS, 252d drawdown <=-10% is DRAWDOWN, else CALM, same 5-day confirmation filter. Thresholds are conventions (the textbook correction definition and the usual elevated-vol level), taken from outside the dataset so they cannot import training-window dependence; where they land in our distribution was reported, not tuned. Stability is perfect, kappa 1.000 — and the pre-registration said in advance that this proves nothing, because a CONSTANT label is also perfectly stable. The test that mattered was discrimination, and it fails: forward 21-day returns are not distinguishable across states (p=0.089), and STRESS is degenerate at 3.5% of days because DRAWDOWN is evaluated first and absorbs most high-vol periods. THE USEFUL DISTINCTION THIS PRODUCES: forward VOLATILITY is cleanly ordered (CALM 12.8% < DRAWDOWN 20.5%), so regime does carry RISK information — it is only RETURN information it lacks. That maps directly onto the live rule book: using regime to scale exposure or size risk has support; using it to modify expected return, which is what the REGISTERED TENSION x0.5 conviction modifier does, does not. Also worth noting DRAWDOWN windows show HIGHER median forward returns (+5.13% vs +1.59%) — the buy-the-dip direction, and not significant on 107 windows.

verdicts.name: REGIME K-SWEEP — retuning the state count does not fix it
verdicts.n: 663 shared days × K=2/3/4 · six full walk-forwards
verdicts.stat: kappa: K=2 0.342 · K=3 0.217 · K=4 0.127 — none reaches the 0.4 line, let alone 0.6
verdicts.note: Follow-up to the training-window instability finding, with the decision rule fixed before running (kappa >=0.6 stable, 0.4-0.6 marginal, <0.4 unstable). The 'fewer states are more stable' hypothesis is directionally correct — kappa rises monotonically as K falls — and nowhere near far enough. K=2's 79.8% raw agreement is the trap: both runs park ~80% of days in one state, so chance alone is 69.3% and almost all of the apparent agreement is arithmetic. RETUNING K IS A CLOSED AVENUE; the overlay needs replacing with a deterministic rule, not tuning. The sweep also reproduced the K=3 result independently (0.217 vs 0.24) from a different data path. Separately it found a defect in run_walkforward_10y.py that I wrote: the model object was not checkpointed, so every resume forced an unscheduled refit off the 21-day grid and the labels depended on where the run was paused. Fixed — checkpoints now only land on refit boundaries, making any chunking identical.

verdicts.name: REGIME DETECTOR — unstable to its own training window
verdicts.stat: best agreement under ANY relabelling 49.8% vs 33.8% chance · Cohen's kappa 0.24
verdicts.note: The walk-forward HMM read a price file starting 2021-12, so after a 500-day warmup it had 33 months of labels — 5 TENSION, 4 DRAWDOWN. Rerunning the IDENTICAL algorithm on the 10-year panel gives 97 months (30 TENSION, 43 DRAWDOWN) and, for the first time, a DRAWDOWN state that has actually seen the COVID crash. But the two runs agree on only 42.5% of the days they share, and the best any of the six state relabellings achieves is 49.8% against 33.8% by chance — kappa 0.24. Over the same 659 days one model spends 77% of its time in one state and the other spends 63% in a different one. Same features, same K, same confirmation filter; only the training length differs. This does not mean regime detection cannot work — it means these LABELS are substantially a function of how much history the model happened to have, and three signals plus the REGISTERED TENSION x0.5 modifier are conditioned on them. It also weakens stress_regime.py, which tested K=2/4 and ablations on the 33-month input and concluded the master variable survived: a stress test run on an underpowered sample is itself underpowered.

verdicts.name: POWER AUDIT — how many of our negatives are actually evidence
verdicts.stat: 4 REAL NEGATIVES · 5 INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered)
verdicts.note: A negative only carries information if the test COULD have found the effect. For each published negative: MDE = 2.80 x SE (the standard 80%-power two-sided 5% constant), compared against what the LITERATURE claims, never against our own estimate. Five of nine could not have detected the published effect if it had been fully present — their 'no' was the only answer available and should be read as INCONCLUSIVE, not as evidence of absence. Score v2 would need 737 formation years and has 10; accruals needs 186 and has 18. That is not an execution failure, it is a property of annual-formation cross-sectional tests, which is why the academic literature uses 50-90 year samples. The practical consequence: stop expecting annual-frequency factor studies to resolve on this data, and spend effort where n can actually grow. Two studies report only a t-statistic with no effect size and cannot be audited at all — itself worth fixing.

verdicts.name: Up-move drift — RESOLVED on the 10-year panel
verdicts.stat: month-clustered CAR20 −0.32% · t −1.16 over 120 months · MDE now 0.77% vs 1.0% literature
verdicts.note: The power audit said this study needed ~38,600 events and had 3,985, so its negative meant nothing. A 10-year daily research panel (2,513 bars per name vs 251, 9.3x the data, standard errors 3.05x tighter) produced 64,311 events — past the requirement — and the answer held. This is now a REAL negative: price-shock drift does not exist here at the size the literature claims. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE FINDING ABOUT THE REGIME OVERLAY: the raw regime split looks dramatic (TENSION up-fade −1.81% t −4.46; DRAWDOWN up-continuation +2.03% t +4.89) and is an artifact. The walk-forward HMM timeline only covers 2023-11 onward — 33 months, of which just 5 are TENSION and 4 are DRAWDOWN. Those thousands of events come from a handful of independent periods, and the study's own clustering guard correctly refused to report them for having fewer than 6 months. The system's MASTER CONDITIONING VARIABLE has 4 validated DRAWDOWN months behind it.

verdicts.name: Residual mean reversion (stat arb, universe scale)
verdicts.note: The stat-arb layer widened from 17 defence names to the whole universe — but NOT as pairwise cointegration, which is indefensible here: 1,584 names give 1.25m pairs (~100k within-sector), so noise alone yields thousands of 'cointegrated' survivors, and 251 daily bars give the ADF step almost no power. Instead one hypothesis tested once: strip leave-one-out market and sector beta, rank the residual, trade the extremes. Turnover is 40%/day at 1d and 90% at 5d, so costs of ~4bp and ~9bp swamp a gross edge that was not significant to begin with. VERIFIED, not asserted: an injection test plants a reversal of strength k into the real panel and the identical pipeline recovers it (k=0.05 → +76.7bp at t 12.1; k=0.15 → +189bp at t 26.7), so the null is the data's and not the code's. Measured residual autocorrelation says the same thing more directly — lag 1 is +0.0003 (t +0.1), exactly the lag traded, while lags 2 and 5 are real but ~1% (t −4.7, −4.3), roughly two orders of magnitude below the cost of harvesting them. Honest correction: the pre-registration predicted the leave-one-out factor correction would matter materially. It did not — self-inclusive factors gave −0.20bp against −0.82bp, both zero. The reasoning was right, the magnitude was not.

verdicts.name: Accruals — RE-RUN with revenue-coherence exclusion
verdicts.note: Second of the two pre-registered re-runs. Accruals are SCALED by revenue, and revenue is a fragment for banks, insurers and REITs, so 813 firm-years were dropped by a rule fixed in advance: drop the firm-year if gross profit, operating cash flow or net income exceeds revenue in that same year. Fails on two independent counts — t = 1.43 against a Bonferroni bar of 2.24, and sign stability 56% against a 60% floor. Worth stating plainly: the exclusion made the result WORSE, not better (was +9.2pt, t 1.51, 61% before), so the mis-scaled names had been mildly FLATTERING the anomaly. Cleaning data is not a way of improving results, and this is what that looks like.

multiple_testing.note: With 20 hypotheses at α=0.05 you expect ~1 false positive by chance. The three CANDIDATEs must therefore clear a board-level bar, not just their own: Bonferroni α=0.0025 (|t| ≈ 3.3), or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 10%. Crash-reversal (month-clustered t=2.04) does NOT clear it and is already flagged below the adopted t≥3 rule. 13D activist drift (t=2.80) does not clear Bonferroni either — it survives on forward-only re-testing, not on its in-sample t. De-escalation reactors are rank-stability, not a t-test, and are judged on the frozen-basket forward clock instead. None of this retracts a result; it states the bar honestly so a lucky one cannot be mistaken for a real one.

survivorship.mechanism: charts/metrics/ratios contain only companies alive today; firms that went bankrupt or were acquired are absent, lifting return levels in every bucket
survivorship.effect: biases LEVELS upward; biases SPREADS between buckets much less, which is why ranked comparisons remain informative and absolute returns do not
survivorship.fix: requires a delisted-securities dataset we do not hold — stated, not solved
